2527.text:
Arrange the following bases in decreasing order of basicity is
(i) Aniline
(ii) O - nitroaniline
(iii) m-& nitroaniline
(iv) p& - nitroaniline
2527.sol:
Basicity is directly proportional to the $+ M, + I$ effect, but it is inversely proportional to the $- M, - I$ effect. Aniline is the highest basic because it does not have any group. But the nitro group can show the $- I$and $- M$ effect. The nitro group at meta position show only the $- I$ effect. But at ortho and para position, it will show the $- M, - I$ effect both. So, the $m -$nitroaniline is more basic than the $p -$nitroaniline and $o -$nitroaniline.

So, the basicity order is :-

Hence, the decreasing order of basicity is $( i ) >( iii )>( iv )>( ii )$.

5336.text: $0 . 63g$ of Oxalic acid is dissolved in order to obtain $250{cm}^{3}$ of its solution. Find the normality of this solution. [Oxalic acid: $\left( COOH{)}_{2} \cdot 2{H}_{2}O\right]$
5336.sol:
Molar mass of oxalic acid =& $126g / mol$

Mole =$\dfrac{Givenmass}{Molarmass} = \dfrac{0 . 63}{126} = 0 . 005mol$

Molarity = $\dfrac{Moleofsolute}{Volumeofsolutioninml} \times 1000 = \dfrac{0 . 005}{250} \times 1000 = 0 . 02M$

Equivalent mass of oxalic acid = $\dfrac{126}{2} = 63$

Gram equivalent of the solute = $\dfrac{0 . 63}{63} = 0 . 01$

$Normality = \dfrac{Gramequivalentofsolute}{Volumeofsolutioninml} \times 1000 = \dfrac{0 . 01}{250} \times 1000 = 0 . 04N$

Hence, normality of solution is $0 . 04N$.

5798.text: The number of positively and negatively charged sols respectively in the following are $\mathrm{TiO}_2$, blood, $\mathrm{CdS}, \mathrm{Cu}, \mathrm{Ag}$, Clay, $\mathrm{SiO}_2, \mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3$.
5798.sol:
( ( ) One of the most important properties of colloidal solutions is that colloidal particles possess a definite type of electrical charge. In a particular colloidal solution, all the colloidal particles carry the same type of charge, while the dispersion medium has an equal but opposite charge. Thus, the charge on colloidal particles is balanced by that of the dispersion medium and the colloidal solution as a whole is electrically neutral.
Positively charged sols are $\mathrm{TiO}_2, \mathrm{CdS}, \mathrm{Fe}_2 \mathrm{O}_3, \mathrm{SiO}_2$ Negatively charged sols are blood, $\mathrm{Cu}, \mathrm{Ag}$, clay.

Given that $\begin{aligned} & \alpha=\sin ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{x}{2}+\frac{\sqrt{3-3 x^2}}{2}\right), 0 < x < \frac{1}{2} \\ & \Rightarrow \alpha=\sin ^{-1} x+\cos ^{-1}\left(\frac{1}{2} \cdot x+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \cdot \sqrt{1-x^2}\right) \end{aligned}$

11542.text: $E_1: a+b+c=0, \quad$ if 1 is a root of $a x^2+b x+c=0, \quad E_2: b^2-a^2=2 a c$, if $\sin \theta$, $\cos \theta$ are the roots of $a x^2+b x+c=0$ Which of the following is true?
11542.sol:
Given that, 1 is a root of $a x^2+b x+c=0\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad a+b+c=0 \\
& \therefore \quad E_1: a+b+c=0 \text{ is true. }
\end{aligned}$
Since $\cos \theta, \sin \theta$ are the roots of
$\begin{aligned}
& a x^2+b x+c=0 \\
\therefore \quad & \sin \theta+\cos \theta=-\frac{b}{a} \\
\text{ and } \sin \theta \cos \theta= & \frac{c}{a}
\end{aligned}$
On squaring both sides of equation (i)
$\begin{array}{rlrl} & (\sin \theta+\cos \theta)^2 & =\frac{b^2}{a^2} \\
\Rightarrow \sin ^2 \theta+\cos ^2 \theta+2 \sin \theta \cos \theta & =\frac{b^2}{a^2} \\
\Rightarrow & 1+2\left(\frac{c}{a}\right) & =\frac{b^2}{a^2} \\
\Rightarrow & 2 \cdot \frac{c}{a} & =\frac{b^2-a^2}{a^2} \\
\Rightarrow & -a^2+b^2 & =2 a c \\
\therefore & E_2: b^2-a^2 & =2 a c \text{ is true }
\end{array}$\Rightarrow E_1$ and $E_2$ both are true.$

&

\end{aligned}$$\therefore \quadstatement II$ is also true.

14708.text:
A particle is kept on the surface of a uniform sphere of mass $1000$ kg and radius $1m$. The work done per unit mass against the gravitational force between them is

$\left[G = 6 . 67 \times {10}^{- 11}Nm^{2}{Kg}^{- 2}\right]$
14708.sol:
Work done by a conservative force is the change in potential energy, therefore, $W = {U}_{f} - {U}_{i}$

Now, the gravitational potential energy per unit mass or gravitational potential of the particle is, $V = - G\dfrac{M}{r}$

So, the initial potential energy, ${V}_{i} = - \left(6. 67 \times {10}^{- 11}\right)\dfrac{1000}{1} = 6. 67 \times {10}^{- 8}J{kg}^{- 1}$

The final potential energy to take the particle far away from the sphere is ${V}_{f} = - G\dfrac{M}{\infty} = 0$

Work done per unit mass of the particle to take it far away from the spare against the gravitational force is,

$W = {V}_{f} - {V}_{i} = 0 - \left(- 6. 67 \times {10}^{- 8}\right)J{kg}^{- 1}W = 6. 67 \times {10}^{- 8}J{kg}^{- 1}$

19881.subject: Chemistry
19881.text: For a given reaction of the type $\dfrac{3}{5} X(a q) \rightarrow \dfrac{1}{2} Y(a q)+Z(g)$, the correct expression for the rate of disappearance of $X$ with reference to $Y$ is $\qquad$
19881.sol:
For a general chemical reaction $aA + bB \rightarrow cC + dD$, the rate of reaction is given by $-\dfrac{1}{a} \dfrac{d[A]}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{b} \dfrac{d[B]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{c} \dfrac{d[C]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{d} \dfrac{d[D]}{dt}$.

Given the reaction $\dfrac{3}{5} X \rightarrow \dfrac{1}{2} Y + Z$, we apply the rate expression:

$-\dfrac{1}{3/5} \dfrac{d[X]}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{1/2} \dfrac{d[Y]}{dt}$

$-\dfrac{5}{3} \dfrac{d[X]}{dt} = 2 \dfrac{d[Y]}{dt}$

Rearranging to solve for the rate of disappearance of $X$, which is $-\dfrac{d[X]}{dt}$:

$-\dfrac{d[X]}{dt} = \dfrac{3}{5} \times 2 \dfrac{d[Y]}{dt}$

$-\dfrac{d[X]}{dt} = \dfrac{6}{5} \dfrac{d[Y]}{dt}$

Answer: $-d \dfrac{[X]}{d t}=+\dfrac{6}{5} d \dfrac{[Y]}{d t}$

19907.text: Given below are graphs showing the variation in velocity constant with temperature on Kelvin scale. Identify the graph which represents Arrhenius equation.
19907.sol:
The Arrhenius equation is $k = Ae^{-\frac{E_a}{RT}}$, where $k$ is the rate constant, $T$ is the temperature in Kelvin, $E_a$ is the activation energy, $R$ is the universal gas constant, and $A$ is the pre-exponential factor.

$k$ vs $T$: As $T$ increases, the exponent $-\dfrac{E_a}{RT}$ becomes less negative, so $k$ increases exponentially with $T$. Graph [B] shows this exponential increase.

Taking natural log: $\ln k = \ln A - \dfrac{E_a}{R}\left(\dfrac{1}{T}\right)$

This is a straight line in $\ln k$ vs $\dfrac{1}{T}$ with negative slope $-\dfrac{E_a}{R}$. Graph [D] shows a positive slope, so it is incorrect.

Graphs [A] and [C] do not match the Arrhenius relationship. Graph [B] is the correct representation.

20652.text:
In the following question a statement of Assertion (A) followed by a statement of Reason (R) is given. Choose the correct option out of the choices given below.
Assertion (A): van't Hoff factor for a solution of benzoic acid in benzene is less than one.
Reason(R): Benzoic acid undergoes dissociation in benzene and its calculated molecular mass using colligative properties is lower than its actual molecular mass.
options: Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are incorrect
Assertion (A) and incorrect and Reason (R) is correct
20652.sol:
Benzoic acid (C_{6}H_{5}COOH$) undergoes dimerization in non-polar solvents like benzene due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding. This association leads to a decrease in the number of particles in the solution.

The van't Hoff factor $i$ is defined as the ratio of observed colligative property to calculated colligative property. For association, $i < 1$. Thus, the Assertion (A) is correct.

The Reason (R) states that benzoic acid undergoes dissociation in benzene, which is incorrect. It undergoes association. Furthermore, for association, the observed colligative property is lower than the calculated one, which implies that the observed molecular mass is higher than the actual molecular mass, not lower. Therefore, the Reason (R) is incorrect.

Answer: Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect$

22134.subject: Mathematics
22134.text: The distance of the point $(1,2)$ from the line $x+y+2=0$ measured along the line parallel to $2 x-y=5$ is equal to
22134.sol:
The given point is $P(1, 2)$ and the line is $L: x + y + 2 = 0$.

The line passing through $P(1, 2)$ and parallel to $2x - y = 5$ has a slope $m = 2$.

The equation of this line is $y - 2 = 2(x - 1)$, which simplifies to $y = 2x$ or $2x - y = 0$.

To find the intersection point $Q$ of $x + y + 2 = 0$ and $2x - y = 0$, we substitute $y = 2x$ into the first equation:

$x + 2x + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow 3x = -2 \Rightarrow x = -\dfrac{2}{3}$.

Then $y = 2(-\dfrac{2}{3}) = -\dfrac{4}{3}$. So, $Q = (-\dfrac{2}{3}, -\dfrac{4}{3})$.

The distance $PQ$ is given by the distance formula:

$PQ = \sqrt{(1 - (-\dfrac{2}{3}))^2 + (2 - (-\dfrac{4}{3}))^2}$

$PQ = \sqrt{(\dfrac{5}{3})^2 + (\dfrac{10}{3})^2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{25}{9} + \dfrac{100}{9}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{125}{9}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{125}}{3} = \dfrac{5\sqrt{5}}{3}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{5 \sqrt{5}}{3}$

22354.text: In a given circuit, the instantaneous values of the alternating voltage and current are $V = 0.5\sin \left(80\pi$ t + $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) volt and $ I = 0.5\sin(80$\pi$ t)$ ampere respectively. Find the average power consumed in that circuit.$
22354.sol:
Given instantaneous voltage $V = 0.5\sin \left(80\pi$ t + $\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) V

Given instantaneous current $ I = 0.5\sin(80$\pi$ t)$ A

Peak voltage $V_0 = 0.5$ V

Peak current $I_0 = 0.5$ A

Phase difference $\phi = $\dfrac{\pi}{3}

Average power consumed in the circuit is given by $ P_{avg} = V_{rms} I_{rms} \cos\phi = $\dfrac{V_0 I_0}{2} \cos\phi

Substituting the values:

$ P_{avg} = $\dfrac{0.5 \times 0.5}{2} \cos \left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)

$ P_{avg} = $\dfrac{0.25}{2} \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{0.25}{4} =0.0625$ W

Answer: $0.0625$ W

23639.subject: Physics
23639.text: In the Young's double slit experiment, when a monochromatic light is used, fringe width obtained is 1 mm. If the wave length is halved and the slit width is doubled, what will be the new fringe width?
23639.sol:
The fringe width $\beta$ in Young's double slit experiment is given by the formula $\beta = \dfrac{\lambda D}{d}$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength of light, $D$ is the distance between the slits and the screen, and $d$ is the distance between the two slits.

Given the initial fringe width $\beta_1 = 1$ mm, we have $\beta_1 = \dfrac{\lambda_1 D}{d_1} = 1$ mm.

According to the problem, the new wavelength $\lambda_2 = \dfrac{\lambda_1}{2}$ and the new slit separation $d_2 = 2d_1$. The distance $D$ remains constant.

The new fringe width $\beta_2$ is given by $\beta_2 = \dfrac{\lambda_2 D}{d_2}$.

Substituting the new values, we get $\beta_2 = \dfrac{(\lambda_1 / 2) D}{2 d_1} = \dfrac{1}{4} \times \dfrac{\lambda_1 D}{d_1}$.

Since $\dfrac{\lambda_1 D}{d_1} = 1$ mm, we have $\beta_2 = \dfrac{1}{4} \times 1$ mm = $0.25$ mm.

Answer: 0.25 mm

25655.text: Let $a and b$ be non-zero and real numbers. Then, the equation $\left(a x^2+b y^2+c\right)\left(x^2-5 x y+6 y^2\right)=0$ represents
options:
Four straight lines, when $c=0$ and $a, b$ are of the same sign

Two straight lines and a circle, when $a=b$ and $c$ is of sign opposite to that of $a$

Two straight lines and a hyperbola, when $a$ and $b$ are of the same sign and $c$ is of sign opposite to that of $a$

A circle and an ellipse, when $a$ and $b$ are of the same sign and $c$ is of sign opposite to that of $a$
25655.sol:
Let $a$ and $b$ be non- zero real numbers.
Therefore, the given equation $\left(a x^2+b y^2+c\right)\left(x^2-5 x y+6 y^2\right)=0$ implies either

$\begin{array}{rc}$& x²-5 x y+6 y²=0 \\
\Rightarrow & (x-2 y)(x-3 y)=0 \\
\Rightarrow & x=2 y $\text{ and }$x=3 y
\end{array}

represent two straight lines passing through origin.
Or $\quad a x^2+b y^2+c=0$
When $c=0$ and $a$ and $b$ are of same signs, then

$\begin{aligned}$& a x²+b y²+c=0 \\
\Rightarrow & x=0 $\text{ and }$y=0
\end{aligned}

which is a point specified as the origin.
When $a=b$ and $c$ is of sign opposite to that of $a, a x^2+b y^2+c=0$ represents a circle.
Hence, the given equation $\left(a x^2+b y^2+c\right)\left(x^2-5 x y+6 y^2\right)=0$
may represent two straight lines and a circle.

25759.subject: Mathematics
25759.text: A ship is fitted with three engines $E_{1}, E_{2}$ and $E_{3}$. The engines function independently of each other with respective probabilities $\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{4}$ and $\frac{1}{4}$. For the ship to be operational at least two of its engines must function. Let $X$ denote the event that the ship is operational and let $X_{1}, X_{2}$ and $X_{3}$ denote respectively the events that the engines $E_{1}, E_{2}$ and $E_{3}$ are functioning. Which of the following is(are) true?
options: $P$ [Exactly two engines of the ship are functioning $[X]=\frac{7}{8}$
25759.sol:
Given that $P\left(X_{1}\right)=\frac{1}{2}, \mathrm{P}\left(X_{2}\right)=\frac{1}{4}, \mathrm{P}\left(X_{3}\right)=\frac{1}{4} P(X)=P$ (at least 2 engines are functioning)

$\begin{aligned}=P\left(X_{1} \cap X_{2}\right.&\left.\cap X_{3}^{C}\right)+P\left(X_{1} \cap X_{2}^{C} \cap X_{3}\right) \\ &+P\left(X_{1}^{C} \cap X_{2} \cap X_{3}\right)+P\left(X_{1} \cap X_{2} \cap X_{3}\right) \end{aligned} =\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{3}{4}+\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{4}$

(a) $P\left(X_{1}^{C} / X\right)=\frac{P\left(X_{1}^{C} \cap X\right)}{P(X)}=\frac{P\left(X_{1}^{C} \cap X_{2} \cap X_{3}\right)}{P(X)} =\frac{\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{4}}{\frac{1}{4}}=\frac{1}{8} \therefore$ (a) is not true.

(b) $P$ [Exactly two engines are functioning $/ X] =\frac{P[(\text{ Exactly two engines are functioning }) \cap X]}{P(X)} =\frac{P\left(X_{1}^{C} \cap X_{2} \cap X_{3}\right)+P\left(X_{1} \cap X_{2}^{C} \cap X_{3}\right)+P\left(X_{1} \cap X_{2} \cap X_{3}^{C}\right)}{P(X)} =\frac{\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{3}{4}}{\frac{1}{4}}=\frac{7}{8} \therefore$ (b) is true.

(c) $P\left(X / X_{2}\right)=\frac{P\left(X \cap X_{2}\right)}{P\left(X_{2}\right)} =\frac{P\left(X_{1} \cap X_{2} \cap X_{3}\right)+P\left(X_{1}^{C} \cap X_{2} \cap X_{3}\right)+P\left(X_{1} \cap X_{2} \cap X_{3}^{C}\right)}{P\left(X_{2}\right)} =\frac{\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{3}{4}}{\frac{1}{4}}=\frac{5}{8} \therefore$ (c) is not true.

(d) $P\left(X / X_{1}\right)=\frac{P\left(X \cap X_{1}\right)}{P\left(X_{1}\right)} =\frac{P\left(X_{1} \cap X_{2} \cap X_{3}\right)+P\left(X_{1} \cap X_{2}^{C} \cap X_{3}\right)+P\left(X_{1} \cap X_{2} \cap X_{3}^{C}\right)}{P\left(X_{1}\right)} =\frac{\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{1}{4}+\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{4} \times \frac{3}{4}}{\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{7}{16} \therefore$ (d) is true.

26197.text: One end of a spring of negligible unstretched length and spring constant $k$ is fixed at the origin $( 0, 0 )$. A point particle of mass $m$ carrying a positive charge $q$ is attached at its other end. The entire system is kept on a smooth horizontal surface. When a point dipole $\overset{\to}{p}$ pointing towards the charge $q$ is fixed at the origin, the spring gets stretched to a length $l$ and attains a new equilibrium position (see figure below). If the point mass is now displaced slightly by $\Deltal ≪ l$ from its equilibrium position and released, it is found to oscillate at frequency $\dfrac{1}{\delta}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}},$ The value of $\delta$ is _______.
26197.sol:
Original frequency $f = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$

If dipole appears,

At equilibrium

$\dfrac{2Kp}{{\left(ℓ + {x}_{0}\right)}^{3}} \cdot q = k{x}_{0} . . . \left(i\right)$

Now disturbed

$\dfrac{2Kp}{{\left(ℓ + {x}_{0} + x\right)}^{3}} \cdot q - k\left({x}_{0} + x\right) = ma$

$⇒ ma = \dfrac{2Kpq}{{\left(ℓ + {x}_{0}\right)}^{3}}{\left[1 + \dfrac{x}{ℓ + {x}_{0}}\right]}^{- 3} - k\left({x}_{0} + x\right)$

$⇒ ma = \dfrac{2Kpq}{{\left(ℓ + {x}_{0}\right)}^{3}}{\left[1 - \dfrac{3x}{ℓ + {x}_{0}}\right]}^{- 3} - k\left({x}_{0} + x\right) = - \dfrac{6Kpqx}{{\left(ℓ + {x}_{0}\right)}^{4}} - kx$

$= - \dfrac{3x}{ℓ + {x}_{0}}k{x}_{0} - kx = - kx\left[\dfrac{3{x}_{0}}{ℓ + {x}_{0}} + 1\right]$

As$ℓ$ is negative,   

$ma = - 4kx$;   $⇒ a = \dfrac{4k}{m}x$

New frequency :

${f}^{'} = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\sqrt{\dfrac{4k}{m}} = 2f$ $= \dfrac{1}{\delta}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$

$∴ \delta = \pi = 3 . 14$

29550.text: The measured $BOD$ values tor four difterent water samples $\left(A - D\right)$ are as tollows: $A = 3$ ppm; $B = 18$ ppm; $C = 21$ ppm; $D = 4$ ppm. The water samples which can be called as highly polluted with organic wastes, are
29550.sol:
The amount of oxygen required by bacteria to break down the organic matter present in a certain volume of a sample of water, is called Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD).

The amount of BOD in the water is a measure of the amount of organic material in the water, in terms of how much oxygen will be required to break it down biologically.

Clean water would have BOD value of less than $5$ ppm whereas highly polluted water could have a BOD value of $17$ ppm or more.

Hence,Among the given samples, sample number B and C are polluted.

$\begin{cases}\alpha & \beta & \gamma & \delta \\ {K}_{H} & 50 & 2 & 2 \times {10}^{- 5} & 0 . 5\end{cases}$

(density of water $= {10}^{3}k{gm}^{- 3}$ at $298K$ ) This table implies that :
options: $\alpha$ has the highest solubility in water at a given pressure
solubility of $\gamma$ at $308K$ is lower than at $298K$
The pressure of a $55 . 5$ molal solution of $\delta$ is $250$ bar
The pressure of $55 . 5$ molal solution of $\gamma$ is $1bar$.
31788.sol:
(1) From Henery's law $P = {k}_{H}\left(X\right)$

Higher the value of ${k}_{H}$ smaller will be solubility so $\gamma$ is more soluble.

(2) Though solubility of gas will decrease with increase in temperature but this conclusion can not be drawn from the given table.

(3)For

$\delta ⇒ {P}_{\delta} = \left({K}_{H \delta}\right) . \left(X\right)\delta$

$= 0 . 5 \times {10}^{3} \times \left[\dfrac{55 . 55}{55 . 55 + \dfrac{1000}{18}}\right] = 250bar .$

(4)For $\gamma$

${\left(p\right)}_{\gamma} = {\left({K}_{H}\right)}_{\gamma} \times {\left(x\right)}_{\gamma}$

$= 2 \times {10}^{- 2}\left[\dfrac{55 . 5}{55 . 5 + \dfrac{1000}{18}}\right] = {10}^{- 2}bar$

32770.text:
In conversion of lime-stone to lime, $\mathrm{CaCO}_3(\mathrm{~s}) \longrightarrow \mathrm{CaO}(\mathrm{s})+\mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{~g})$
the vales of $\Delta \mathrm{H}^{\circ}$ and $\Delta \mathrm{S}^{\circ}$ are $+179.1 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ and $160.2 \mathrm{~J} / \mathrm{K}$ respectively at $298 \mathrm{~K}$ and $1\mathrm{~bar}$. 
Assuming that $\Delta \mathrm{H}^{\circ}$ do not change with temperature, temperature above which conversion of limestone to lime will be spontaneous is
32770.sol:
We know, $\Delta \mathrm{G}=\Delta \mathrm{H}-\mathrm{T} \Delta \mathrm{S}$
So, lets find the equilibrium temperature, i.e. at which
$\begin{aligned}
& \Delta \mathrm{G}=0 \\
& \Delta \mathrm{H}=\mathrm{T} \Delta \mathrm{S} \\
& \mathrm{T}=\frac{179.1 \times 1000}{160.2} \\
& =1118 \mathrm{~K}
\end{aligned}$
So, at temperature above this, the reaction will become spontaneous. Hence, (D) is correct answer.

33261.text: Let $A = \left\{x \in R: \left|x + 1\right| < 2\right\}$ and $B = \left\{x \in R: \left|x - 1\right| \ge 2\right\}$. Then which one the following statements is NOT true?
33261.sol:
Given,

$A = \left\{x \in R: \left|x + 1\right| < 2\right\}$

$⇒ A = \left(- 3, 1\right)$

Now, $B = \left\{x \in R: \left|x - 1\right| \ge 2\right\}$

$⇒ B = ( - \infty , - 1 ] ∪ [ 3, \infty )$

Now, $B - A = ( - \infty , - 3 ] ∪ [ 3, \infty )$

$⇒ B - A = R - \left(- 3, 3\right)$

So, option $B$ is not true.

33583.text: Let the line $L: \sqrt{2}x + y = \alpha$ pass through the point of the intersection $P$(in the first quadrant)of the circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 3$ and the parabola ${x}^{2} = 2y$. Let the line $L$ touch two circles ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ of equal radius $2\sqrt{3}$. If the centres ${Q}_{1}$ and ${Q}_{2}$ of the circles ${C}_{1}$ and ${C}_{2}$ lie on the $y -$axis, then the square of the area of the triangle $P{Q}_{1}{Q}_{2}$ is equal to _________.
33583.sol:
Given: ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 3$ and ${x}^{2} = 2y$

$⇒ {y}^{2} + 2y - 3 = 0$

$⇒ \left(y + 3\right)\left(y - 1\right) = 0$

$⇒ y = 1, - 3\left(\text{Rejected as it gives imaginary value of}x\right)$

$⇒ y = 1$

$⇒ x = \sqrt{2}$

$⇒ P ≡ \left(\sqrt{2}, 1\right)$

Now, $P$ lies on the line $\sqrt{2}x + y = \alpha$.

$⇒ \sqrt{2}\left(\sqrt{2}\right) + 1 = \alpha$

$⇒ \alpha = 3$

For circle ${C}_{1}$, ${Q}_{1}$ lies on $y -$axis.

Let ${Q}_{1} ≡ \left(0, \beta\right)$ and ${R}_{1} = 2\sqrt{3}$ (given)

Line $L$ act as tangent so applying the condition of tangency

$⇒ P = r$

$⇒ \left|\dfrac{\beta - 3}{\sqrt{3}}\right| = 2\sqrt{3}$

$⇒ \left|\beta - 3\right| = 6$

$⇒ \beta - 3 = 6, - 6$

$⇒ \beta = 9, - 3$

So, ${Q}_{1} ≡ \left(0, 9\right) \text{ and } {Q}_{2} ≡ \left(0, - 3\right)$

$⇒ Ar\left(\DeltaP{Q}_{1}{Q}_{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left|\begin{array}{ll}\sqrt{2} \\ 0 \\ 0\end{array} \begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 9 \\ - 3\end{array} \begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{array}\right|$

$⇒ Ar\left(\DeltaP{Q}_{1}{Q}_{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\sqrt{2}\left(12\right)\right)$

$⇒ Ar\left(\DeltaP{Q}_{1}{Q}_{2}\right) = 6\sqrt{2}$

$⇒ {\left(\DeltaP{Q}_{1}{Q}_{2}\right)}^{2} = 72$

35350.text: Let a vertical tower $AB$ have its end $A$ on the level ground. Let $C$ be the mid-point of $AB$ and $P$ be a point on the ground such that  $AP = 2AB$. If $∠BPC = \beta$, then $tan\beta$ is equal to:
35350.sol:
Let $∠ APC = \alpha$
Given, $AB = 2\left(AC\right) = 2\left(BC\right)$

Also $AP = 2AB ⇒ AP = 4\left(AC\right) = 4\left(BC\right)$

$⇒ tan\alpha = \dfrac{AC}{AP} = \dfrac{AC}{4\left(AC\right)} = \dfrac{1}{4}$

$⇒ tan\left(\alpha + \beta\right) = \dfrac{AB}{AP} = \dfrac{AB}{2\left(AB\right)} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Let, $tan\beta = x$

$\dfrac{tan\alpha + tan\beta}{1 - tan\alpha ⋅ tan\beta} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{4} + x}{1 - \dfrac{x}{4}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1 + 4x}{4 - x} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$⇒ 2 + 8x - 4 + x = 0$

$⇒ 9x - 2 = 0$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{2}{9}$

36048.text: Let $x = \left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{array}\right]$ and $A = \left[\begin{cases}- 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & - 1\end{cases}\right]$. For $k \in \mathbb{N}$, if ${X}^{'}{A}^{k}X = 33$, then $k$ is equal to
36048.sol:
Given,

$X = \left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{array}\right] \text{ and } A = \left[\begin{cases}- 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & - 1\end{cases}\right]$

Also given, ${X}^{T}{A}^{K}X = 33$

Now putting the value of matrices in ${X}^{T}{A}^{K}X = 33$ we get,

$\left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1\end{cases}\right]{\left[\begin{cases}- 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & - 1\end{cases}\right]}^{k}\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{array}\right] = 33$

Now finding ${A}^{2} = \left[\begin{cases}- 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & - 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}- 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & - 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

And ${A}^{4} = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 12 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

Similary ${A}^{8} = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 24 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

And ${A}^{10} = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 24 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 30 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

So, for $K \to$ Even ${A}^{K} = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 3K \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$

Now again putting the value in ${X}^{T}{A}^{K}X = 33$ we get,

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 3K \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{array}\right] = 33$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 3K + 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{array}\right] = 33$

$⇒ \left[3K + 3\right] = 33$

Now assuming $33$ as $\left[33\right]$

We get, $3K + 3 = 33 ⇒ K = 10$

Now, if $K$ is odd ${X}^{T}{A}^{K}X = 33$

We can rewrite above expression as ${X}^{T}A{A}^{K - 1}X = 33$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}1 & 1 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}- 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 0 & - 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 & 0 & 3k - 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{array}\right] = 33$

$⇒ \left[\begin{cases}- 1 & 3 & 8\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{array}{ll}3k - 2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{array}\right] = \left[33\right]$

$⇒ \left[- 3k + 13\right] = \left[33\right]$

$⇒ k = 20 / 3$ (not possible)

So, $k = 10$ is the required answer.

36341.text: Let ABC be a triangle. Consider four points $\mathrm{p}_{1}, \mathrm{p}_{2}, \mathrm{p}_{3}, \mathrm{p}_{4}$ on the side AB, five points $p_{5}, p_{6}, p_{7}, p_{8}, p_{9}$ on the side $B C$, and four points $p_{10}, p_{11}, p_{12}, p_{13}$ on the side AC. None of these points is a vertex of the triangle ABC. Then the total number of pentagons, that can be formed by taking all the vertices from the points $\mathrm{p}_{1}, \mathrm{p}_{2}, \ldots, \mathrm{p}_{13}$, is $\_\_\_\_$
36341.sol:
Points: 4 on AB, 5 on BC, 4 on AC. For a valid pentagon, no 3 vertices can be collinear, so at most 2 points from each side.
Only valid distribution $(a, b, c)$ with $a+b+c = 5$ and each $\le 2$ is permutations of $(1, 2, 2)$:
$(1,2,2)$: $\binom{4}{1}\binom{5}{2}\binom{4}{2} = 4 \cdot 10 \cdot 6 = 240$
$(2,1,2)$: $\binom{4}{2}\binom{5}{1}\binom{4}{2} = 6 \cdot 5 \cdot 6 = 180$

37624.text: The mean of $5$ observations is $5$ and their variance is $12 . 4$. If three of the observations are $1, 2 \text{ and } 6$; then the value of the remaining two is :
37624.sol:
$\dfrac{x + y + 1 + 2 + 6}{5} = 5$

$⇒ x + y = 16$

Now $12.4 = \dfrac{\left(16 + 9 + 1 + {\left(x - 5\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - 5\right)}^{2}\right)}{5}$

$⇒ 62= 26 + {\left(x - 5\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - 5\right)}^{2}$

$⇒ 36 = {\left(x - 5\right)}^{2} + {\left(y - 5\right)}^{2}$

Shifting of the origin to $\left(5, 5\right)$ the equations will become

${6}^{2} = {x}^{2} + {y}^{2} and x + y = 6$

Solving them and again will get the $x = 0 or y = 0$.

If $x = 0 ⇒ y = 6$ or

If $y = 0 ⇒ x = 6$.

But by shifting the origin back to original position, we get $x = 0 + 5 = 5 \text{ and } y = 6 + 5 = 11$

(or)

$x = 6 + 5 = 11 \text{$ and } y = 0 + 5 = 5

Hence, the values of the remaining two are $5, 11$.

38069.text: A vector $\overset{\to}{a}$ is parallel to the line of intersection of the plane determined by the vectors $\overset{^}{i}, \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$ and the plane determined by the vectors $\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}, \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}$. The obtuse angle between $\overset{\to}{a}$ and the vector $\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$ is
38069.sol:
The normal to the plane determined by the vectors $\overset{^}{i}, \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$ will be

$\overset{\to}{n}1 = \overset{^}{i} \times \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}\right) = \overset{^}{k}$

The normal to the plane determined by the vectors $\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}, \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}$ will be

$\overset{\to}{n}2 = \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{k}\right) \times \left(\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right)$

$= \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}$

Now the vector along the line of intersection will be $\overset{\to}{n}1 \times \overset{\to}{n}2$

$= \overset{^}{k} \times \left(\overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j} - \overset{^}{k}\right) = - \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$

i.e. $\overset{\to}{a} = - \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$

Given $\overset{\to}{b} = \overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}$

$\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b} = - 3$

Let $\left(\overset{\to}{a} ∧ \overset{\to}{b}\right) = \theta$

Now $cos\theta = \dfrac{\overset{\to}{a} \cdot \overset{\to}{b}}{\left|\overset{\to}{a}\right|\left|\overset{\to}{b}\right|} = \dfrac{- 3}{\sqrt{2} \times 3}$

$\theta = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$

Given line is parallel to the line $x + y - z = 0 = x - 2y + 3z - 5$ is:

So, direction ratio of the line $= \left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 1 & - 1 \\ 1 & - 2 & 3\end{cases}\right| = \overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}$

So, equation of line passing through $\left(1, 2, 4\right)$ is

$\overset{\to}{r} = \overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + 4\overset{^}{k} + \lambda \left(\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}\right)

Let A\left(1, 2, 4\right),$Q$\left(1, - 2, 5\right)$ and P be $\left(1 + \lambda, 2 - 4\lambda, 4 - 3\lambda\right)$

Given $\overset{\to}{PQ}$ and line are perpendicular,

So, $\overset{\to}{PQ} \cdot \left(\overset{^}{i} - 4\overset{^}{j} - 3\overset{^}{k}\right) = 0$

$⇒ \lambda = \dfrac{13}{26} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

38337.subject: Mathematics
38337.text: The sum of all values of $x$ in $[ 0, 2\pi ]$, for which $sinx + sin2x + sin3x + sin4x = 0$, is equal to :
38337.sol:
Given,

$sinx + sin2x + sin3x + sin4x = 0$

$⇒ ( sinx + sin4x ) + ( sin2x + sin3x ) = 0$

$⇒ 2sin\dfrac{5x}{2}cos\dfrac{3x}{2} + 2sin\dfrac{5x}{2}cos\dfrac{x}{2} = 0$

$⇒ 2sin\dfrac{5x}{2}\left\{cos\dfrac{3x}{2} + cos\dfrac{x}{2}\right\} = 0$

$⇒ 2sin\dfrac{5x}{2}\left\{2cosxcos\dfrac{x}{2}\right\} = 0$

$2sin\dfrac{5x}{2} = 0 ⇒ \dfrac{5x}{2} = 0, \pi, 2\pi, 3\pi, 4\pi, 5\pi$

$⇒ x = 0, \dfrac{2\pi}{5}, \dfrac{4\pi}{5}, \dfrac{6\pi}{5}, \dfrac{8\pi}{5}, 2\pi$

and $cos\dfrac{x}{2} = 0 ⇒ \dfrac{x}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} ⇒ x = \pi$

and $cosx = 0 ⇒ x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{3\pi}{2}$

So sum $= 6\pi + \pi + 2\pi = 9\pi$

39349.text: A particle of mass $m$ is dropped from a height $h$ above the ground. At the same time another particle of the same mass is thrown vertically upwards from the ground with a speed of $\sqrt{2gh} .$ If they collide head-on completely inelastically, the time taken for the combined mass to reach the ground, in units of $\sqrt{\dfrac{h}{g}}$ is:
39349.sol:
time for collision ${t}_{1} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2gh}}$
After ${t}_{1}$
${V}_{A} = 0 - g{t}_{1} = - \sqrt{\dfrac{gh}{2}}$
and ${V}_{B} = \sqrt{2gh} - g{t}_{1} = \sqrt{gh}\left[\sqrt{2} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right]$
at the time of collision
${\overset{\to}{p}}_{i} = \overset{\to}{{p}_{f}}$
$⇒ m{\overset{\to}{V}}_{A} + m{\overset{\to}{V}}_{B} = 2m{\overset{\to}{V}}_{f}$
$⇒ - \sqrt{\dfrac{gh}{2}} + \sqrt{gh}\left[\sqrt{2} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right] = 2{\overset{\to}{V}}_{f}$
${V}_{f} = 0$

and height from ground

$= h - \dfrac{1}{2}g{t}_{1}^{2} = h - \dfrac{h}{4} = \dfrac{3h}{4}$

so time ,

$t = \sqrt{2 \times \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{3h}{4}\right)}{g}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}\sqrt{\dfrac{h}{g}}$

40171.text: The energy of an electromagnetic wave contained in a small volume oscillates with
options: Double the frequency of the wave
Half the frequency of the wave
40171.sol:
The formula to calculate the energy confined within the electric component of an electromagnetic wave can be written as

${u}_{E} = \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}{E}^{2}dV . . . \left(1\right)$

Let's assume that the equation of the electric component is given by

$E = {E}_{0}sin\left(\omegat + ϕ\right) . . . \left(2\right)$

Substitute the expression for the electric field component from equation (2) into equation (1) and simplify to obtain the expression for the energy confined within the small volume $dV$.

$\begin{cases}{u}_{E} & = & \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}{\left[{E}_{0}sin\left(\omegat + ϕ\right)\right]}^{2}dV \\ & = & \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}{{E}_{0}}^{2}\sin^{2}\left(\omegat + ϕ\right)dV \\ & = & \dfrac{1}{4}{ε}_{0}{{E}_{0}}^{2}\left[1 - cos\left(2\omegat + 2ϕ\right)\right] . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

From equation (3), it can be concluded that the frequency of oscillation of the energy confined within a small volume is double the frequency of the wave.

41195.subject: Physics
41195.text: A mass of $1\text{ kg}$ is kept on an inclined plane with $30°$ inclination with respect to horizontal plane and it is at rest initially. Then the whole assembly is moved up with constant velocity of $4\text{ m/s}$. The work done by the frictional force in time $2\text{ s}$ is _______ J. (Take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$)
41195.sol:
Since the assembly moves with a constant velocity, the acceleration of the mass is zero. The mass is in equilibrium relative to the incline.

The frictional force $f$ acting on the mass balances the component of gravity along the inclined plane. Therefore, the magnitude of the frictional force is:

$f = mg \sin 30^\circ$

Substituting the given values ($m = 1\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$):

$f = 1 \times 10 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 5\text{ N}$

The direction of the frictional force is upwards along the incline. Since the incline makes an angle of $30^\circ$ with the horizontal, the frictional force makes an angle of $90^\circ - 30^\circ = 60^\circ$ with the vertical upward direction.

The displacement $s$ of the assembly in time $t = 2\text{ s}$ is vertically upwards:

$s = vt = 4 \times 2 = 8\text{ m}$

The work done by the frictional force is:

$W = f s \cos 60^\circ$

$W = 5 \times 8 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = 20\text{ J}$

Answer: $20$

The formula for Young's modulus is given by:

$Y = \dfrac{F L_0}{A \Delta L} = \dfrac{4 F L_0}{\pi d^2 \Delta L}$

Substituting the given values into the formula:

$Y = \dfrac{4 \times 100 \times 1.5}{\pi \times (0.08 \times 10^{-2})^2 \times (0.5 \times 10^{-2})}$

$Y = \dfrac{600}{\pi \times 64 \times 10^{-8} \times 5 \times 10^{-3}} = \dfrac{15}{8\pi} \times 10^{11} \text{ N/m}^2$

The relative error in Young's modulus is:

$\dfrac{\Delta Y}{Y} = \dfrac{\Delta L_0}{L_0} + 2\dfrac{\Delta d}{d} + \dfrac{\Delta (\Delta L)}{\Delta L}$

Substituting the least counts as absolute errors and the measured values:

$\dfrac{\Delta Y}{Y} = \dfrac{0.1}{150} + 2 \times \dfrac{0.001}{0.08} + \dfrac{0.001}{0.5}$

$\dfrac{\Delta Y}{Y} = \dfrac{1}{1500} + \dfrac{1}{40} + \dfrac{1}{500}$

$\dfrac{\Delta Y}{Y} = \dfrac{2 + 75 + 6}{3000} = \dfrac{83}{3000}$

The absolute error in Young's modulus is:

$\Delta Y = Y \times \dfrac{\Delta Y}{Y} = \left(\dfrac{15}{8\pi} \times 10^{11}\right) \times \dfrac{83}{3000}$

$\Delta Y = \dfrac{15 \times 83}{24000 \pi} \times 10^{11} = \dfrac{83}{1600 \pi} \times 10^{11} = \dfrac{83}{16\pi} \times 10^9 \text{ N/m}^2$

Using $\pi \approx 3.14$:

$\Delta Y = \dfrac{83}{16 \times 3.14} \times 10^9 = \dfrac{83}{50.24} \times 10^9 \approx 1.65 \times 10^9 \text{ N/m}^2$

Comparing this with $\alpha \times 10^9 \text{ N/m}^2$, we get $\alpha = 1.65$.

Answer: $1.65$

42154.text: A cube of metal is subjected to a hydrostatic pressure $4GPa$. The percentage change in the length of the side of the cube is close to : (Given bulk modulus of metal, $B = 8 \times {10}^{10}Pa$)
42154.sol:
$B = - \dfrac{∆ P}{\dfrac{∆ V}{V}}$
$\dfrac{∆ V}{V} = - \dfrac{∆ P}{B}$
Magnitude is given by,
$\left|\dfrac{∆ V}{V}\right| = \dfrac{∆ P}{B}$

Volume in terms of length can be represented as,

$3 \times \left|\dfrac{∆ L}{L}\right| = \dfrac{∆ P}{B}$

Therefore,

$\left|\dfrac{∆ L}{L}\right| = \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{∆ P}{B}$

Substituting the values we get,
$\left|\dfrac{∆ L}{L}\right| = \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{4 \times {10}^{9}}{8 \times {10}^{10}} = \dfrac{1}{60}$

Percantage change is,
$\dfrac{1}{60} \times 100 = \dfrac{5}{3} = 1 . 67$

42943.text: If the refractive index of the material of a prism is $cot\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)$, where $A$ is the angle of prism then the angle of minimum deviation will be

The formula to calculate the refractive index $\left(\mu\right)$ of the material of the prism is given by

$\mu = \dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{A + {\delta}_{m}}{2}\right)}{sin\left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)} . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

$cot\dfrac{A}{2} = \dfrac{sin\left(\dfrac{A + {\delta}_{m}}{2}\right)}{sin\dfrac{A}{2}}$

$⇒ cos\dfrac{A}{2} = sin\left(\dfrac{A + {\delta}_{m}}{2}\right) ⇒ sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{A}{2}\right) = sin\left(\dfrac{A + {\delta}_{m}}{2}\right)$

$⇒ \dfrac{A + {\delta}_{m}}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{A}{2}$

$⇒ {\delta}_{m} = \pi - 2A$

43167.text: A solid sphere of mass 5 kg and radius 10 cm is kept in contact with another solid sphere of mass 10 kg and radius 20 cm. The moment of inertia of this pair of spheres about the tangent passing through the point of contact is $\_\_\_\_$ $\mathrm{kg}. \mathrm{m}^{2}$.

Sphere 1: $m_1 = 5$ kg, $r_1 = 0.1$ m
Sphere 2: $m_2 = 10$ kg, $r_2 = 0.2$ m
For a solid sphere, $I_{cm} = \frac{2}{5}mr^2$
The tangent at contact is perpendicular to the line joining centers. The perpendicular distance from each sphere's center to this tangent line equals its radius.
Using parallel axis theorem: $I_{total} = I_{cm} + md^2$
For sphere 1: $I_1 = \frac{2}{5}(5)(0.1)^2 + 5(0.1)^2 = 0.02 + 0.05 = 0.07$ kg·m²
For sphere 2: $I_2 = \frac{2}{5}(10)(0.2)^2 + 10(0.2)^2 = 0.16 + 0.4 = 0.56$ kg·m²
Total: $I = 0.07 + 0.56 = 0.63$ kg·m²

43740.subject: Physics
43740.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion $A$ and the other is labelled as Reason $R$.

Assertion $A$ : When a rod lying freely is heated, no thermal stress is developed in it.

Reason $R$ : On heating, the length of the rod increases.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both $A$ and $R$ are true and $R$ is the correct explanation of $A$
Both $A$ and $R$ are true but $R$ is NOT the correct explanation of $A$
43740.sol:
Thermal stress is mechanical stress created by any change in temperature of a material. When the body is under some constraints, thermal stress is generated. But if it is lying freely, no thermal stress is developed.

The increase in length of a body with temperature is given by

$∆ L = L\alpha ∆ T$

So, with the increase in temperature, the length of the rod increases.

$A$ and $R$ are true but $R$ is not the correct explanation of $A$.

44250.text: When a polaroid sheet is rotated between two crossed polaroids then the transmitted light intensity will be maximum for a rotation of :
44250.sol:
Let ${I}_{0}$ be intensity of unpolarised light incident on first polaroid.
${I}_{1} =$ Intensity of light transmitted from ${1}^{\text{st}}$ polaroid
$= \dfrac{{I}_{0}}{2}$
If $\theta$ be the angle between ${1}^{\text{st}}$ and ${2}^{\text{nd}}$ polaroid and $ϕ$ be the angle between ${2}^{\text{nd}}$ and ${3}^{\text{rd}}$ polaroid, then

$\theta + ϕ = 90 ° . . . \left(1\right)$

If ${I}_{2} =$ Intensity from ${2}^{\text{nd}}$ polaroid,

$\begin{cases}{I}_{2} & = & {I}_{1}co{s}^{2}\theta \\ & = & \dfrac{{I}_{0}}{2}co{s}^{2}\theta\end{cases}$

If ${I}_{3} =$ Intensity from ${3}^{\text{rd}}$ polaroid

$\begin{cases}{I}_{3} & = & {I}_{2}co{s}^{2}ϕ \\ & = & {I}_{1}\cos^{2}\theta\cos^{2}ϕ \\ & = & \dfrac{{I}_{0}}{2}co{s}^{2}\thetaco{s}^{2}\left(90 ° - \theta\right) \\ & = & \dfrac{{I}_{0}}{2}co{s}^{2}\thetasi{n}^{2}\theta \\ & = & \dfrac{{I}_{0}}{2}{\left[\dfrac{2sin\thetacos\theta}{2}\right]}^{2} \\ & = & \dfrac{{I}_{0}}{8}\sin^{2}2\theta\end{cases}$

Now, ${I}_{3}$ will be maximum when

$sin2\theta = 1$

$⇒ 2\theta = 90 °$

$⇒ \theta = 45 °$

Here, $\gamma=49 \times 19^{-5}{ }^{\circ} \mathrm{C}^{-1}$
$\begin{aligned} \Delta \mathrm{T} & =30^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \mathrm{V}^{\prime} & =\mathrm{V}+\Delta \mathrm{V}=\mathrm{V}(\mathrm{l}+\gamma \Delta \mathrm{T})\end{aligned}$

For a transistor, \(\beta\)-current gain and \(\alpha\)-current gain are related as
\[\$beta=\frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha}$\]
Given, \(\alpha\)-current gain \( =0.98 \)
Therefore, \(\$beta=\frac{0.98}{1-0.98}=\frac{0.98}{0.02}=$49 \)
\(\beta\)-current gain of transistor is \( 49 \).

56278.text: Identify the term used for drugs that reduce or relieve pain without causing loss of consciousness.
56278.sol:
Analgesics are neurological active drugs that reduce or abolish pain without causing impairment of consciousness, mental confusion, incoordination or paralysis or some other disturbances of nervous system.

Antipyretics are chemical substances which reduce body temperature during high fever.

Antibiotics are chemical substances produced wholly or partly by chemical synthesis, which in low concentrations inhibit the growth or destroy microorganisms by intervening in their metabolic processes.

Antimicrobials tend to destroy/prevent development or inhibit the pathogenic action of microbes such as bacteria, fungi, virus or other parasites selectively.

Answer: Analgesic

57567.sol:
The reaction of an aryl halide with sodium metal in the presence of dry ether to form biphenyl is known as the Fittig reaction.

$2\text{Ar-X} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{Ar-Ar} + 2\text{NaX}$

The Wurtz reaction involves two alkyl halides to form an alkane, while the Wurtz-Fittig reaction involves one alkyl halide and one aryl halide to form an alkylarene. The Swarts reaction is used for the synthesis of alkyl fluorides.

Answer: Fittig reaction

61683.text:
Derivative of
$\mathrm{y}=\sqrt{\sin x+\sqrt{\sin x+\sqrt{\sin x+\ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots \ldots}} \infty}$ is
61683.sol:
Given the infinite nested radical

$y = \sqrt{\sin x + \sqrt{\sin x + \sqrt{\sin x + \cdots}}}$

which satisfies the relation

$y^2 = \sin x + y$

after squaring both sides.

Differentiate implicitly with respect to $x$, noting that $y$ is a function of $x$:

$2y \frac{dy}{dx} - \frac{dy}{dx} - \cos x = 0$

Factor to isolate $\frac{dy}{dx}$:

$\frac{dy}{dx}(2y - 1) = \cos x$

Solving for the derivative yields:

$\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{\cos x}{2y - 1}$

This matches option D, confirming the result.

62919.subject: Mathematics
62919.text:
Consider the following statements.
$p$: If $3^4 > 4^3$, then $3^3 > 4^4$
$q$: The roots of the equation $x^2 - 2x + 2 = 0$ are real if and only if Mumbai is in Maharashtra.
$r$: Statement $p$ is true or statement $q$ is false.
Which of the following has truth value T (true)?
62919.sol:
Evaluate the truth value of statement $p$:
$3^4 = 81$ and $4^3 = 64$, so $3^4 > 4^3$ is True (T).
$3^3 = 27$ and $4^4 = 256$, so $3^3 > 4^4$ is False (F).
Statement $p$ is of the form $T \rightarrow F$, which is False. Thus, $p \equiv F$.

Evaluate the truth value of statement $q$:
The discriminant of $x^2 - 2x + 2 = 0$ is $D = 4 - 8 = -4 < 0$, so the roots are not real. This part is False (F).
"Mumbai is in Maharashtra" is True (T).
Statement $q$ is of the form $F \leftrightarrow T$, which is False. Thus, $q \equiv F$.

Evaluate the truth value of statement $r$:
"Statement $p$ is true" is False (since $p \equiv F$).
"Statement $q$ is false" is True (since $q \equiv F$).
Statement $r$ is of the form $F \vee T$, which is True. Thus, $r \equiv T$.

Now, check the truth values of the given options:
$(p \vee q) \wedge r \equiv (F \vee F) \wedge T \equiv F \wedge T \equiv F$
$p \vee (q \wedge r) \equiv F \vee (F \wedge T) \equiv F \vee F \equiv F$
$p \wedge (q \vee r) \equiv F \wedge (F \vee T) \equiv F \wedge T \equiv F$
$(p \wedge q) \vee r \equiv (F \wedge F) \vee T \equiv F \vee T \equiv T$

Therefore, $(p \wedge q) \vee r$ has the truth value T.

Answer: $(p \wedge q) \vee r$

64221.text: From the following options, the nearest line to the origin is....
64221.sol:
Nearest Line to the Origin

A line is nearest to the origin if it has the smallest perpendicular distance from the origin, calculated by $d = |C| / \sqrt{A^2 + B^2}$ for the standard form $Ax + By + C = 0$.

For $3x - 4y + 4 = 0$: $d = |4| / \sqrt{9 + 16} = 4/5 = 0.8$

For $2x - 3y - 5 = 0$: $d = | -5 | / \sqrt{4 + 9} \approx 5 / 3.605 \approx 1.387$

For $4x - 3y + 12 = 0$: $d = |12| / \sqrt{16 + 9} = 12/5 = 2.4$

For $5x - 2y - 3 = 0$: $d = | -3 | / \sqrt{25 + 4} \approx 3 / 5.385 \approx 0.557$

Distances: 0.8, 1.387, 2.4, 0.557. The least is approximately $0.557$.

The line $5x - 2y = 3$ is nearest to the origin.

65062.text: Let $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{k}, \vec{b} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, and $\vec{c} = 4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$. If $\vec{r}$ is a vector such that $\vec{r} \times \vec{b} = \vec{c} \times \vec{b}$ and $\vec{r} \cdot \vec{a} = 0$, Then $\vec{r} \cdot \vec{c} =$
65062.sol:
Given $\vec{r} \times \vec{b} = \vec{c} \times \vec{b}$

$(\vec{r} - \vec{c}) \times \vec{b} = 0$

$\vec{r} - \vec{c} = \lambda \vec{b}$

$\vec{r} = \vec{c} + \lambda \vec{b}$

Taking the dot product with $\vec{a}$:

$\vec{r} \cdot \vec{a} = \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a} + \lambda (\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a}) = 0$

Calculating the dot products:

$\vec{c} \cdot \vec{a} = (4)(2) + (-3)(0) + (7)(1) = 15$

$\vec{b} \cdot \vec{a} = (1)(2) + (1)(0) + (1)(1) = 3$

Substituting these values:

$15 + 3\lambda = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = -5$

Thus, $\vec{r} = \vec{c} - 5\vec{b}$

$\vec{r} = (4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}) - 5(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = -\hat{i} - 8\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$

Now, calculating $\vec{r} \cdot \vec{c}$:

$\vec{r} \cdot \vec{c} = (-\hat{i} - 8\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}) \cdot (4\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 7\hat{k})$

$\vec{r} \cdot \vec{c} = -4 + 24 + 14 = 34$

Answer: $34$

65558.text:
Alternating current of peak value $\left(\dfrac{2}{\pi}\right)$ A flows through the primary coil of a transformer. The coefficient of mutual inductance between primary and secondary coils is 1H. The peak value of induced e.m.f. in the secondary coil is
(Frequency of a.c. = 50 Hz)
65558.sol:
The current in the primary coil is $I = I_0 \sin(\omega t)$.

The induced e.m.f. in the secondary coil is given by $e = -M \dfrac{dI}{dt}$.

$e = -M \dfrac{d}{dt} (I_0 \sin(\omega t)) = -M I_0 \omega \cos(\omega t)$

The peak value of the induced e.m.f. is $e_0 = M I_0 \omega$.

Given $M = 1$ H, $I_0 = \dfrac{2}{\pi}$ A, and $f = 50$ Hz.

The angular frequency is $\omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \times 50 = 100\pi$ rad/s.

Substituting the values, we get:

$e_0 = 1 \times \left(\dfrac{2}{\pi}\right) \times 100\pi = 200$ V.

Answer: $200\text{V}$

65610.subject: Physics
65610.text: In an a.c. circuit containing $L, C$ and $R$ in series, the ratio of apparent power to the true power is (Z and R are the impedance and resistance respectively, $\phi=$ phase angle)
65610.sol:
Apparent power $S$ in an a.C. circuit is $S = V_{\text{rms}} I_{\text{rms}}$, or equivalently $S = I_{\text{rms}^2 Z$, where $Z$ is the circuit's impedance.

True power $P$ represents the actual power dissipated and is given by $P = V_{\text{rms}} I_{\text{rms}} \cos \phi$, where $\phi$ is the phase angle between voltage and current, or $P = I_{\text{rms}^2 R$, with $R$ being the resistance.

The ratio of apparent to true power is

$\frac{S}{P} = \frac{V_{\text{rms}} I_{\text{rms}}}{V_{\text{rms}} I_{\text{rms}} \cos \phi} = \frac{1}{\cos \phi}$.

Given that the power factor is $\cos \phi = \frac{R}{Z}$, then

$\frac{1}{\cos \phi} = \frac{Z}{R}$.

Alternatively, starting from the current-based expressions:

$\frac{S}{P} = \frac{I_{\text{rms}^2 Z}{I_{\text{rms}^2 R} = \frac{Z}{R}$.

Thus, the ratio is $\frac{Z}{R}$, which corresponds to option D.

Final answer: $\boxed{D}$

66063.text: Five capacitors, each of capacity 'C' are connected as shown in the figure. The resultant capacity between A & B is $14 \mu \mathrm{ F}$. The capacity of each capacitor is
66063.sol:
The upper branch comprises three identical capacitors of capacitance $C$ in parallel, producing $C_{\text{upper}} = C + C + C = 3C$.

In the lower branch, two such capacitors are in series, yielding an equivalent capacitance given by $\frac{1}{C_{\text{lower}}} = \frac{1}{C} + \frac{1}{C} = \frac{2}{C}$, so $C_{\text{lower}} = \frac{C}{2}$.

Between points A and B, these two branches are in parallel, resulting in total capacitance $C_{AB} = 3C + \frac{C}{2} = \frac{7C}{2}$.

Given $C_{AB} = 14\, \mu\mathrm{F}$, we solve $\frac{7C}{2} = 14$, leading to $7C = 28$ and thus $C = 4\, \mu\mathrm{F}$.

The capacity of each capacitor is $4\, \mu\mathrm{F}$.

66538.subject: Physics
66538.text: If the kinetic energy of a particle is increased to 16 times, the percentage change in the de Broglie wavelength of a particle is
66538.sol:
The de Broglie wavelength of a particle is given by $\lambda = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$, where $K$ is the kinetic energy.

Let the initial kinetic energy be $K_1 = K$ and the initial wavelength be $\lambda_1 = \lambda$.

The final kinetic energy is given as $K_2 = 16K$.

The final wavelength is $\lambda_2 = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2m(16K)}} = \dfrac{1}{4} \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}} = \dfrac{\lambda}{4}$.

The percentage change in the de Broglie wavelength is $\dfrac{\lambda_2 - \lambda_1}{\lambda_1} \times 100\%$.

Substituting the values, we get $\dfrac{\dfrac{\lambda}{4} - \lambda}{\lambda} \times 100\% = -\dfrac{3}{4} \times 100\% = -75\%$.

The magnitude of the percentage change is $75\%$.

Answer: $75\ \%$

67399.subject: Physics
67399.text: According to law of equipartition of energy the molar specific heat of a non rigid diatomic gas at constant volume is
67399.sol:
For a non-rigid diatomic gas, the degrees of freedom are distributed as follows:

Translational degrees of freedom = $3$
Rotational degrees of freedom = $2$
Vibrational degrees of freedom = $2$ (since each vibrational mode contributes to both kinetic and potential energy)

Total degrees of freedom $f = 3 + 2 + 2 = 7$

According to the law of equipartition of energy, the internal energy per mole of the gas is given by:

$U = \dfrac{f}{2}RT = \dfrac{7}{2}RT$

The molar specific heat at constant volume is:

$C_v = \dfrac{dU}{dT} = \dfrac{7}{2}R$

Answer: $(7/2) R$

68692.subject: Physics
68692.text:
$A simple pendulum is suspended from ceiling of a lift when lift is at rest its period is 'T'. With what acceleration 'a' should lift be accelerated upward in order to reduce the period to ' \frac{\mathrm{T}}{2}$ ?
(take 'g' as acceleration due to gravity)
68692.sol:
The period of a simple pendulum is $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g_{\text{eff}}}}$, where $L$ is the length and $g_{\text{eff}}$ is the effective gravitational acceleration.

When the lift is at rest, $g_{\text{eff}} = g$, so the period is $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}$.

If the lift accelerates upward with acceleration $a$, the effective gravity becomes $g + a$, yielding a new period $T' = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g + a}}$.

Given that $T' = \frac{T}{2}$, substitute the expressions:

$\frac{1}{2} \cdot 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g + a}}$

Simplify and square both sides:

$\frac{L}{g} = 4 \cdot \frac{L}{g + a}$

Cancel $L$ and solve for $a$:

$g + a = 4g$

$a = 3g$

The lift must accelerate upward at $3g$.

71061.subject: Biology
71061.text: The individual transitional communities during ecological succession are called ________ communities.
71061.sol:
Ecological succession is the gradual and fairly predictable change in the species composition of a given area.

The entire sequence of communities that successively change in a given area is called a sere.

The individual transitional communities that develop during this process are termed seral stages or seral communities.

The first community to inhabit an area is called the pioneer community, while the final, stable community that is in near equilibrium with the environment is called the climax community.

Therefore, the individual transitional communities are called seral communities.

Answer: seral

Chloromycetin (also known as chloramphenicol) is an antibiotic isolated from the soil bacterium Streptomyces venezuelae. Thus, A matches with III.

Erythromycin is a macrolide antibiotic produced by the actinomycete Streptomyces erythreus. Thus, B matches with IV.

Griseofulvin is an antifungal medication derived from the fungus Penicillium griseofulvum. Thus, C matches with I.

Terramycin belongs to the tetracycline group of antibiotics. While typically associated with Streptomyces rimosus, in the context of the given options, it is matched with Streptomyces aureofaciens (which produces the closely related chlortetracycline). Thus, D matches with II.

The correct matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

71373.subject: Biology
71373.text: A normal woman whose father was colourblind is married to a normal man, (assuming equal distribution of female gametes), then _________.
options: $50\%$ of their sons will be colourblind.
All the sons will be colourblind.
All the sons will be normal.
$75\%$ of the sons will be colourblind.
71373.sol:
Colour blindness is an X-linked recessive trait.

Let $X^C$ be the normal allele and $X^c$ be the allele for colour blindness.

The woman's father was colourblind (X^c Y$), so he passed the $X^c$ chromosome to her. Since she is normal, her genotype is $X^C X^c$ (carrier).

The normal man has the genotype $X^C Y$.

A cross between the carrier woman (X^C X^c$) and the normal man (X^C Y$) produces the following offspring:

Daughters: $X^C X^C$ (normal) and $X^C X^c$ (normal carrier).

Sons: $X^C Y$ (normal) and $X^c Y$ (colourblind).

Since the sons receive their X chromosome from the mother, who produces $X^C$ and $X^c$ gametes in equal proportions, 50\%$ of the sons will be normal and $50\%$ will be colourblind.

Answer: $50\%$ of their sons will be colourblind.

Rust occurs when metals containing iron react with the oxygen in the air or in water and form a compound called iron(III) oxide (ferric oxide). This compound contains water molecules, so we call it a hydrated compound. Both oxygen gas and water must be present for the iron to rust. Chemically and very simply speaking, iron atoms lose a few electrons to oxygen atoms. This process by which electrons are removed from atoms is called oxidation. 74663.text:
When you walk on a woolen carpet and bring your finger
near the metallic handle of a door an electric shock is
produced. This is because
options: charge is transferred from your body to the handle
a chemical reaction occurs when you touch the handle
the temperature of the human body is higher than that of the handle
the human body and the handle arrive at thermal equilibrium by the process
74663.sol:
All materials are made up of negatively- and positivelycharged particles. These usually exist in equal amounts, balancing each other out. But when two materials come into contact, one may 'steal' negatively-charged
electrons from the other. One material ends up with more negative charges than positive ones, meaning that it becomes negatively-charged overall, whilst the other becomes positively-charged. If the charges cannot move away as they are produced, they accumulate in the material as static charge, or electricity. Once you have built up a big enough static charge, an electric shock is almost inevitable. The moment you touch a conducting material such as metal, the excess electrons jump between your hand and the conductor, giving you a shock.

77090.text: What are the order and degree respectively of the differential equation whose solution is $\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{cx}+\mathrm{c}^2-3 \mathrmc^{3 / 2}+2$, where c is a parameter?
77090.sol:
Given :
Solution of differential equation is
$y=c x+c^2-3 c^{\frac{3}{2}}+2$...(1)
To find order and degree of differential equation, we will find differential equation first.
Now differentiating equation (1) w.r.t. $x$ and putting value of $c$ to remove it, we get
$\frac{d y}{d x}=c\begin{aligned} & y=x \frac{d y}{d x}+\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2-3\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^{\frac{3}{2}}+2 \\ & \Rightarrow(y-2)^2+\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^4+(2 x-9)\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^3\end{aligned}+\left(x^2-2 y+4\right)\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)^2+(-2 x y+4 x) \frac{d y}{d x}=0$
Hence order of differential equation is 1 and degree is 4 .

80407.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: During aerobic respiration, the role of oxygen is limited to the terminal stage.
In ETC (Electron Transport Chain), one molecule of NADH $+ {H}^{+}$ gives rise to $2$ ATP molecules, and one ${FADH}_{2}$ gives rise to $3$ ATP molecules.
Oxidation-reduction reactions produce proton gradients in respiration.
80407.sol:
Aerobic respiration is the process that leads to the complete oxidation of organic substances in the presence of oxygen and releases ${CO}_{2},$ water, and a large amount of energy present in the substrate. The crucial events in aerobic respiration are:

  • The complete oxidation of pyruvate by the stepwise removal of all the hydrogen atoms, leaving three molecules of ${CO}_{2}$
  • The passing on of the electrons removed as part of the hydrogen atoms to molecular ${O}_{2}$ with the simultaneous synthesis of ATP.

When the electrons pass from one carrier to another via complex I to IV in the electron transport chain, they are coupled to ATP synthase (complex V) to produce ATP from ADP and inorganic phosphate. The number of ATP molecules synthesised depends on the nature of the electron donor. Oxidation of one molecule of NADH gives rise to 3 molecules of ATP, while that of one molecule of ${FADH}_{2}$ produces $2$ molecules of ATP. Although the aerobic process of respiration takes place only in the presence of oxygen, the role of oxygen is limited to the terminal stage of the process.

82915.text: A very long conducting wire is bent in a semi- circular shape from $A$ to $B$ as shown in figure. The magnetic field at point$P$ for steady current configuration is given by:
82915.sol:
Let's consider the following diagram:

The formula to calculate the magnetic field $\left(\overset{\to}{B}1\right)$ due to wire 1 is given by

$\overset{\to}{B}1 = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\piR} ⊗ . . . \left(1\right)$

The formula to calculate the magnetic field $\left(\overset{\to}{B}2\right)$ due to wire 2 is given by

$\overset{\to}{B}2 = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4R} ⊙ . . . \left(2\right)$

And, the formula to calculate the magnetic field $\left(\overset{\to}{B}3\right)$ due to wire 3 is given by

$\overset{\to}{B}3 = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\piR} ⊗ . . . \left(3\right)$

Hence, the net magnetic field at P can be written as

$\begin{cases}\overset{\to}{B} & = & \overset{\to}{B}1 + \overset{\to}{B}2 + \overset{\to}{B}3 \\ = & \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\piR} ⊗ + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4R} ⊙ + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4\piR} ⊗ \\ = & \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2\piR} ⊗ + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4R} ⊙ \\ = & - \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{2\piR} ⊙ + \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4R} ⊙ \\ = & \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}i}{4R}\left[1 - \dfrac{2}{\pi}\right] ⊙\end{cases}$

84216.subject: Zoology
84216.text:
Which of the following statements related to pituitary gland are correct ?
(a) It is divided anatomically into adenohypophysis and neurohypophysis
(b) It secretes follicle stimulating hormone
(c) It secretes melanocyte stimulating hormone
(d) It does not secrete prolactin
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
84216.sol:
The pituitary gland is anatomically divided into the adenohypophysis and the neurohypophysis. Thus, statement (a) is correct.

The adenohypophysis consists of the pars distalis and the pars intermedia. The pars distalis (anterior pituitary) secretes several hormones, including Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) and Prolactin (PRL). Thus, statement (b) is correct and statement (d) is incorrect.

The pars intermedia secretes Melanocyte Stimulating Hormone (MSH). Thus, statement (c) is correct.

Therefore, statements (a), (b), and (c) are correct.

85296.subject: Zoology
85296.text: In which mode of inheritance do you expect more maternal influence among the offspring?
85296.sol:
During fertilisation, mother contribute its nucleus as well as the cytoplasm. However, father sperm consist only nucleus. Thus, the cytoplasmic inheritance is also called maternal inheritance. Genes located on Y-chromosome show Y-linked inheritance. This carries the paternal influences. A gene located in the X-chromosome shows $\mathrm{X}$-linked inheritance. In this, a male transmits his X-chromosome only to his daughters while a female transmits one of her X-chromosomes to the offspring of both sexes. Autosomes are contributed by both of the parents.
Related Theory
The female reproductive cell or the egg has a large amount of cytoplasm containing many organelles such as chloroplasts and mitochondria which contain their own genes and can reproduce independently. Because these organelles are contributed by the female, cytoplasmic inheritance occurs in the maternal line.

85919.subject: Biology
85919.text:
The ability of phloem to distribute sugar depends on the companion cell and sieve element working as a complex. Consider the following statements with regard to possible effects of reduction in companion cell plasmodesmata.
(i) Sugar loading into sieve tubes reduces due to collapse in osmotic pressure gradient.
(ii) Water moves from companion cells into the xylem to maintain osmotic balance.
(iii) The sieve tubes collapse structurally due to loss of turgor pressure.
(iv) Reverse loading of sugar in phloem begins immediately due to pressure inversion.
Under the given condition, the correct statements are:
85919.sol:
Companion cells and sieve tube elements function together as a complex to load and transport sugars in the phloem. Sugars are loaded from companion cells into sieve tubes through plasmodesmata.

If there is a reduction in companion cell plasmodesmata, the transfer of sugars into the sieve tubes is hindered. This leads to a significant decrease in sugar loading, which in turn causes a collapse in the osmotic pressure gradient that normally draws water into the phloem.

Due to the reduced solute concentration in the sieve tubes, less water enters from the adjacent xylem. This results in a severe drop in turgor pressure within the sieve tubes, which can cause them to structurally collapse.

Statements (ii) and (iv) are incorrect as water does not move from companion cells to xylem to maintain balance, and reverse loading due to pressure inversion does not occur. Thus, statements (i) and (iii) correctly describe the physiological consequences.

Answer: (i) and (iii)

86726.subject: Physics
86726.text: Two protons are separated by a distance of $1$ nanometer. The magnitudes of gravitational, electromagnetic and strong nuclear forces between them are denoted by $F_G$, $F_E$ and $F_S$ respectively. Select the correct option.
86726.sol:
Distance between protons, $r = 1$ nm $= 10^{-9}$ m.

The strong nuclear force is a short-range force and is effective only up to distances of the order of $1$ fm ($10^{-15}$ m). At a distance of $1$ nm, the strong nuclear force is practically zero. Thus, $F_S \approx 0$.

The electromagnetic force between two protons is given by $F_E = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0} \dfrac{e^2}{r^2}$.

The gravitational force between two protons is given by $F_G = G \dfrac{m_p^2}{r^2}$.

The ratio of electromagnetic to gravitational force between two protons is independent of distance and is approximately $10^{36}$. Therefore, $F_E > F_G$.

Since $F_G$ is non-zero and $F_S$ is zero at this distance, we have $F_G > F_S$.

Combining these, the correct order of magnitudes is $F_E > F_G > F_S$.

Answer: $F_E > F_G > F_S$

ii. If $AB$ is removed, assuming the equivalent resistance between remaining resistors is $x,$

$\dfrac{1}{{R}_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{R} + \dfrac{1}{x}$

${R}_{eq} = \dfrac{Rx}{R + x}$

$∴ \dfrac{5}{9} = \dfrac{1 ( x )}{1 + x} = \dfrac{x}{1 + x} . . . . \left(∵ R = 1Ω\right)$

$∴ 5 ( 1 + x ) = 9x$

$∴ 5 + 5x = 9x$

$∴ 5 = 4x$

$∴ x = \dfrac{5}{4}Ω$

$∴ x = 1 . 25Ω$

96421.text: Based on a 10% law of energy transfer, identify values for A, B, and C in the figure given below.
96421.sol: The 10% law was proposed by Lindemann in 1942. The transfer of energy from one trophic level to another trophic level is accompanied by loss of energy at each level or step. When the plants are eaten by the herbivore, approximately 10% of energy in the food is fixed into animal flesh, whereas 90% is consumed in ingestion, respiration, maintenance of body heat and other activities. Similarly, when a carnivore consumes that herbivore, again approimately 10% of energy is fixed. Therefore, at each transfer, only 10% of the total energy is actually available to the next trophic level. It is called 10% law.

97484.subject: Botany
97484.sol: Gymnosperm (gymnos - naked and Sperma - seed) are plants in which ovules are not enclosed by ovary wall and remain exposed both before and after fertilization. The seeds that develop post-fertilization are not covered, are naked. This is a very important character of gymnosperm. In angiosperms, the ovules are present inside the ovary attached to the placenta. Pteridophytes do not have ovules.& Meiospores are formed inside sporangia. Depending upon spore differentiation plants are homosporous (similar spores) and heterosporous (with two type of spores), smaller male microspores and larger female megaspores. Sporangia are associated with leaves called sporophylls.

97515.subject: Botany
97515.text: In Pinus, gametophytic generation is represented by
options: More than one option is correct
97515.sol:
The gymnosperms are heterosporous; they produce haploid microspores and megaspores. The two kinds of spores are produced within sporangia that are borne on sporophylls which are arranged spirally along an axis to form lax or compact strobili or cones. The strobili bearing microsporophylls and microsporangia are called microsporangiate or male strobili. The microspores develop into a male gametophytic generation which is highly reduced and is confined to only a limited number of cells. This reduced gametophyte is called a pollen grain. The development of pollen grains take place within the microsporangia. The cones bearing megasporophylls with ovules or megasporangia are called macrosporangiate or female strobili. The male or female cones or strobili may be
borne on the same tree like in& Pinus.

100897.subject: Physics
100897.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): If water is pumped out of a hose pipe of constant cross-sectional area, the mechanical power required is proportional to the square of the ejection velocity.

Reason (R): The force required to eject the water stream is proportional to the square of its ejection velocity.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
100897.sol:
For a hose pipe of constant cross-sectional area $A$, the mass of water ejected per unit time is $\dfrac{dm}{dt} = \rho A v$, where $\rho$ is the density of water and $v$ is the ejection velocity.

The force required to eject the water is equal to the rate of change of momentum of the water stream:
$F = v \dfrac{dm}{dt} = v(\rho A v) = \rho A v^2$

Thus, $F \propto v^2$. Therefore, the Reason (R) is true.

The mechanical power required by the pump is the product of force and velocity:
$P = Fv = (\rho A v^2)v = \rho A v^3$

Thus, $P \propto v^3$. The Assertion (A) states that power is proportional to the square of the velocity, which is false.

Hence, (A) is false but (R) is true.

Answer: (A) is false but (R) is true

101389.subject: Physics
101389.text:
The mass and radius of four hypothetical planets A, B, C and D are given below in terms of the mass ($M$) and radius ($R$) of the Earth:
Planet A: Mass $M$, Radius $R$
Planet B: Mass $2M$, Radius $R/2$
Planet C: Mass $4M$, Radius $2R$
Planet D: Mass $8M$, Radius $4R$

Which of these planets has the highest escape velocity for an object on its surface?
101389.sol:
The escape velocity of a planet is given by $v_e = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}$, which means $v_e \propto \sqrt{\dfrac{M}{R}}$.

Calculating the ratio $\dfrac{M}{R}$ for each planet:
For Planet A: $\dfrac{M}{R} = 1$
For Planet B: $\dfrac{2M}{R/2} = 4$
For Planet C: $\dfrac{4M}{2R} = 2$
For Planet D: $\dfrac{8M}{4R} = 2$

Since Planet B has the highest value of the ratio $\dfrac{M}{R}$, it yields the highest value for $\sqrt{\dfrac{M}{R}}$ and thus the highest escape velocity.

Answer: Planet B

101738.text: Neglecting the density of air, the terminal velocity obtained by a raindrop of radius $0.3 \mathrm{~mm}$ falling through air of viscosity $18 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~N} \mathrm{~s} \mathrm{~m}^{-2}$ will be

101878.subject: Physics
101878.text: Two slabs of different materials are connected in parallel between two temperature reservoirs. Both slabs have the same uniform thickness. The first slab has a cross-sectional area $A$ and thermal conductivity $K$. The second slab has a cross-sectional area $2A$ and thermal conductivity $3K$. What is the equivalent thermal conductivity of the composite parallel combination?
101878.sol:
For a parallel combination of thermal conductors, the total rate of heat flow is the sum of the individual rates of heat flow:
$H_{eq} = H_1 + H_2$

Let $\Delta T$ be the temperature difference and $L$ be the thickness of the slabs.

The equivalent thermal conductivity $K_{eq}$ is defined for the total area $A_{eq} = A_1 + A_2 = A + 2A = 3A$.

$\dfrac{K_{eq} (3A) \Delta T}{L} = \dfrac{K_1 A_1 \Delta T}{L} + \dfrac{K_2 A_2 \Delta T}{L}$

Substituting the given values:
$K_{eq} (3A) = K(A) + (3K)(2A)$

$3 K_{eq} A = KA + 6KA$

$3 K_{eq} A = 7KA$

$K_{eq} = \dfrac{7K}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{7K}{3}$

103281.subject: Physics
103281.text: Ten identical cells, each of emf $2\text{ V}$ and internal resistance $0.5\ \Omega$, are connected in series to form a battery. However, two of the cells are connected with reverse polarity. If this battery is connected across an external resistor of $5\ \Omega$, the steady current flowing through the circuit will be
103281.sol:
Total number of cells, $n = 10$

Number of reversed cells, $m = 2$

When $m$ cells are reversed out of $n$ cells, the effective emf of the series combination is given by:
$E_{\text{eff}} = (n - 2m)E = (10 - 2 \times 2) \times 2\text{ V} = 6 \times 2\text{ V} = 12\text{ V}$

The internal resistance of the cells is independent of their polarity. Thus, the total internal resistance is:
$r_{\text{eq}} = n \times r = 10 \times 0.5\ \Omega = 5\ \Omega$

The total resistance of the circuit is the sum of the external resistance $R$ and the equivalent internal resistance $r_{\text{eq}}$:
$R_{\text{total}} = R + r_{\text{eq}} = 5\ \Omega + 5\ \Omega = 10\ \Omega$

According to Ohm's law, the steady current $I$ is:
$I = \dfrac{E_{\text{eff}}}{R_{\text{total}}} = \dfrac{12}{10}\text{ A} = 1.2\text{ A}$

Answer: $1.2\text{ A}$

103848.subject: Physics
103848.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : The direction of induced current is always such as to oppose the change that causes it.
Reason (R) : The direction of induced current is given by Lenz's law.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
103848.sol:
- Assertion (A) states that the direction of induced current always opposes the change that causes it. This is a direct statement of Lenz's Law, which is a fundamental principle of electromagnetic induction. So, Assertion (A) is true.
- Reason (R) states that the direction of induced current is given by Lenz's law. This is also a true statement, as Lenz's Law explicitly defines the direction of induced current in a way that aligns with the principle of energy conservation (by opposing the change).
- Furthermore, Reason (R) directly explains why Assertion (A) is true. Lenz's law dictates the opposing nature of the induced current.
Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

104290.text: A transparent, non-magnetic medium has a dielectric constant of $2.25$. What is the speed of light in this medium? (Take the speed of light in vacuum as $3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$)
104290.sol:
For a non-magnetic medium, the relative permeability is approximately unity ($\mu_r = 1$).

The speed of light in a material medium is given by the relation:
$v = \dfrac{c}{\sqrt{\mu_r \epsilon_r}}$

Substituting the given values ($\epsilon_r = 2.25$, $\mu_r = 1$, $c = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$):
$v = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{\sqrt{1 \times 2.25}}$

$v = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{1.5} = 2 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$

Answer: $2 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$

104463.text: Two thin lenses of powers $+12 \text{ D}$ and $-2 \text{ D}$ are placed in contact coaxially. An object is placed at a distance of $15 \text{ cm}$ from this combination. The linear magnification produced by the combination is
104463.sol:
Effective power of the combination, $P_{\text{net}} = P_1 + P_2$

$P_{\text{net}} = +12 \text{ D} + (-2 \text{ D}) = +10 \text{ D}$

Effective focal length, $f_{\text{net}} = \dfrac{100}{P_{\text{net}}} \text{ cm} = \dfrac{100}{10} \text{ cm} = +10 \text{ cm}$

Given object distance, $u = -15 \text{ cm}$ (using sign convention)

Using the formula for linear magnification in terms of focal length and object distance:

$m = \dfrac{f_{\text{net}}}{f_{\text{net}} + u}$

$m = \dfrac{10}{10 + (-15)} = \dfrac{10}{-5} = -2$

Thus, the linear magnification produced is $-2$.

Answer: $-2$

104866.subject: Physics
104866.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The radius of the second stationary orbit of the Be$^{3+}$ ion is equal to the Bohr radius of the hydrogen atom.

Reason (R): The radius of the $n^{\text{th}}$ Bohr orbit is directly proportional to $n$ and inversely proportional to $Z$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
104866.sol:
The radius of the $n^{\text{th}}$ Bohr orbit of a hydrogen-like species is given by:
$r_n = a_0 \dfrac{n^2}{Z}$
where $a_0$ is the Bohr radius of the hydrogen atom ($n=1, Z=1$).

For the Be$^{3+}$ ion, $Z = 4$. The radius of its second stationary orbit ($n = 2$) is:
$r = a_0 \dfrac{2^2}{4} = a_0 \dfrac{4}{4} = a_0$
Thus, the radius of the second orbit of Be$^{3+}$ is exactly equal to the Bohr radius of the hydrogen atom. Therefore, Assertion (A) is true.

The formula shows that the radius is directly proportional to the square of the principal quantum number ($n^2$) and inversely proportional to the atomic number ($Z$). Therefore, Reason (R) is false.

Hence, Assertion is true but Reason is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

105004.subject: Physics
105004.text:
A nucleus containing $Z$ protons has a measured radius of $3.6 \text{ fm}$. If the constant $R_0$ is taken as $1.2 \text{ fm}$, what is the mass number $A$ of this nucleus, and which of the following expressions correctly represents its mass defect $\Delta m$?
(Given: $m_p$ is the mass of a proton, $m_n$ is the mass of a neutron, and $M$ is the rest mass of the nucleus)
options: $A = 3$ and $\Delta m = [Z m_p + (3 - Z) m_n] - M$
$A = 27$ and $\Delta m = M - [Z m_p + (27 - Z) m_n]$
$A = 9$ and $\Delta m = [Z m_p + (9 - Z) m_n] - M$
$A = 27$ and $\Delta m = [Z m_p + (27 - Z) m_n] - M$
105004.sol:
The radius of a nucleus is given by the formula:
$R = R_0 A^{1/3}$

Substitute the given values:
$3.6 = 1.2 A^{1/3}$
$A^{1/3} = \dfrac{3.6}{1.2} = 3$

Cubing both sides, we get the mass number:
$A = 3^3 = 27$

The mass defect $\Delta m$ is the difference between the sum of the masses of the constituent nucleons and the rest mass of the nucleus.
Number of protons = $Z$
Number of neutrons = $A - Z = 27 - Z$

Therefore, the mass defect is:
$\Delta m = [Z m_p + (27 - Z) m_n] - M$

Answer: $A = 27$ and $\Delta m = [Z m_p + (27 - Z) m_n] - M$

114931.subject: Chemistry
114931.text:
The half-life of a first-order reaction is $40 \text{ minutes}$ at $27^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ and $10 \text{ minutes}$ at $47^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. Calculate the activation energy of the reaction.

(Given: $\mathrm{R} = 8.314 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~K}^{-1} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$, $\log 4 = 0.6021$)
114931.sol:
For a first-order reaction, the rate constant $k$ is inversely proportional to the half-life $t_{1/2}$:
$k = \dfrac{0.693}{t_{1/2}}$

Therefore, the ratio of rate constants is:
$\dfrac{k_2}{k_1} = \dfrac{(t_{1/2})_1}{(t_{1/2})_2} = \dfrac{40}{10} = 4$

Convert temperatures to Kelvin:
$T_1 = 27^{\circ} \mathrm{C} + 273 = 300 \mathrm{~K}$
$T_2 = 47^{\circ} \mathrm{C} + 273 = 320 \mathrm{~K}$

Using the Arrhenius equation:
$\log \left(\dfrac{k_2}{k_1}\right) = \dfrac{E_a}{2.303 \mathrm{R}} \left(\dfrac{T_2 - T_1}{T_1 T_2}\right)$

$\log(4) = \dfrac{E_a}{2.303 \times 8.314} \left(\dfrac{320 - 300}{300 \times 320}\right)$

$0.6021 = \dfrac{E_a}{19.147} \left(\dfrac{20}{96000}\right)$

$E_a = \dfrac{0.6021 \times 19.147 \times 96000}{20}$

$E_a = 0.6021 \times 19.147 \times 4800$

$E_a = 55336.6 \mathrm{~J} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1} = 55.34 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$

Answer: $55.34 \mathrm{~kJ} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$

Thus, dissociation of the complex, $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right] \mathrm{Cl}_3$ takes place as follows $\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right] \mathrm{Cl}_3 \longrightarrow\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{NH}_3\right)_6\right]^{2+}+3 \mathrm{Cl}^{-}$
Therefore, total number of ions obtain will be 4 .
117872.meta: How many ions obtain after dissociation of this complex [Co(NH_3)_6] Cl_3 ?

118808.subject: Chemistry
118808.text:
Phenol is treated with aqueous sodium hydroxide followed by carbon dioxide gas, and the resulting mixture is acidified to give compound X. Compound X is then heated with acetic anhydride in the presence of a catalytic amount of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to yield compound Y.

Identify the final product Y.
118808.sol:
In the first step, phenol reacts with sodium hydroxide and carbon dioxide followed by acidification. This is Kolbe's reaction, which yields salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid) as compound X.

In the second step, salicylic acid (X) undergoes acetylation when treated with acetic anhydride in the presence of concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$. The phenolic $-\text{OH}$ group is acetylated to form acetylsalicylic acid, which is commonly known as aspirin (compound Y).

If the first step had been the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, the intermediate would be salicylaldehyde, leading to 2-acetoxybenzaldehyde upon acetylation. Reaction of salicylic acid with methanol would yield methyl salicylate.

Answer: Aspirin

121293.subject: Botany
121293.text: What is the accumulation of diatom cell wall deposits over billions of years referred to as?
121293.sol: This group includes diatoms and golden algae (desmids). They are found in fresh water as well as in marine environments. They are microscopic and float passively in water currents (plankton). Most of them are photosynthetic. In diatoms the cell walls form two thin overlapping shells, which fit together as in a soap box. The walls are embedded with silica and thus the walls are indestructible. <mark style="background-color: yellow, turquious;"> Thus, diatoms have left behind large amount of cell wall deposits in their habitat; this accumulation over billions of years is referred to as ‘diatomaceous earth’. </mark>  Being gritty this soil is used in polishing, filtration of oils and syrups. Diatoms are the chief ‘producers’ in the oceans.
